newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain heralds ETA arrest as another step to peace.
newsitem.headline: Spain heralds ETA arrest as another step to peace.

text.p: Spain on Friday greeted France's arrest of one of the most wanted leaders of Basque separatist guerrilla group ETA as another step toward peace in the troubled Basque region.

The arrest of Jose Luis Urrusolo came as welcome relief on a day when emotions were running high in Spain as thousands took to the streets calling for the release of a prison officer now held by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) for a year.

"This is a significant move toward peace because Urrusolo played an important role within ETA. He is not only the most callous terrorist of all but he is also the most famous," Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja told a news conference.

French police arrested Urrusolo, armed with a handgun and carrying false papers, in Bordeaux on Thursday night. After being stopped at a routine road check he drove off at speed but was caught by police.
"This does not mean the end of the group. We still have a long way to go before this violence ends," Mayor Oreja warned.
Urrusolo, one of ETA's top three leaders, is thought to have been involved in the killing of over 16 people.
Known as the "terrorist of a thousand faces", police say the 39-year old was involved in two of ETA's longest kidnappings, and spent recent years training ETA members.
"You have achieved a great coup, I am a key ETA member," Urrusolo was reported by French police to have said when he was arrested.
Spanish radio reported that the High Court had begun proceedings for the extradition of Urrusolo.
News of the arrest came on the first anniversary of ETA's kidnapping of prison officer Jose Antonio Ortega.
Thousands protested throughout Spain calling for his release, and the government reiterated that it would not be forced into talks demanded by the guerrilla group.

"We must not give the impression that the terrorists are going to get their own way with this blackmail that they are using not only against the Ortega family but also the government and Spanish society," Mayor Oreja told local radio.

On Friday, as part of its fight against the group, the Interior Ministry slapped up thousands of posters on the walls of public places throughout Spain with pictures of the eight alleged ETA members most active in recent months.
ETA has killed 800 people since 1968 in its bid for an independent Basque state, using bombs and shootings alongside kidnappings and extortion to finance itself.

Cooperation between France and Spain has led to more than 200 arrests in the past decade. Earlier this week, France handed over former ETA leader Josu Arkauz to Spanish police after he completed a prison sentence in France.
